body.statement: Testing \(\mathsf C\) on all \(2^{T(T+1)/2}\) bundle designs and deleting every success that strictly contains another success returns exactly \(\mathfrak F(T,S,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)\). Moreover, sufficiency is monotone: if \(B\le B'\) and \(\mathsf C(T,S,B,(|\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\), then \(\mathsf C(T,S,B',( |\mathcal X_t|)_{t=1}^T)=1\).
body.justification: The focal design object is the complete antichain of minimal sufficient measurement bundles, not a single sufficient protocol.
body.gap: Existing monotone-MNAR and double-sampling results fix the observed or recovered record and do not enumerate minimal partial-recovery designs.
body.consumer: Investigators can compare only irreducible protocols when assigning the costs of chart abstraction, laboratory assays, or tracing interviews.

obligation.what_is_open: Monotonicity and enumeration for the frozen certificate criterion await the equality of that criterion with graphwise identification.
obligation.obstruction: Audit marginalization proves monotonicity of graphwise identification, but the frozen statement is about \(\mathsf C\), whose behavior is not fixed until the missing procedure and completeness theorem are supplied.
obligation.attempted: I proved the larger-bundle marginalization argument and counted the admissible bundle inclusions exactly; I then isolated the sole unavailable substitution \(\mathsf C=\operatorname{GID}\).
obligation.partial_result:
Monotonicity is already provable at the graphwise-identification level.
Suppose \(B\le B'\) and two laws have the same observed law under \(B'\).
By audit-table equivalence their \(B'\)-pattern tables agree.  Marginalizing
each table over the coordinates in \(B'_d\setminus B_d\) produces the
corresponding \(B\)-pattern table, so those tables agree as well.  A second
application of audit-table equivalence gives equality of the observed laws
under \(B\).  Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B)=1
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{GID}(T,S,B')=1.
\]
Once \(\mathsf C=\operatorname{GID}\) is established, the same implication
holds for \(\mathsf C\).  There are
\[
2^{\sum_{d=0}^{T-1}(T-d)}=2^{T(T+1)/2}
\]
designs, because each of the \(T(T+1)/2\) admissible pairs \((d,j)\) is
included or excluded independently.  Filtering all successes by strict
coordinatewise inclusion then equals the defining set \(\mathfrak F\).
Thus only the unavailable identification equivalence prevents closure of
the frozen criterion-level statement.
